analysis:
Scope: docs/reference/protocol-messages.md, a documentation-only change. The changed ranges are the "Last updated" date (line 3), an added Swift-only optional `detail` field on the autopilot status table (head ~854), a Swift-only `hold_seconds` field on the autopilot control table (head ~1208), and further additions at head 1355-1380 and 1470-1472. The supplied units are BASE text only, covering base lines 1-581. The head additions at ~854, ~1208, ~1355-1380 and ~1470-1472 fall outside that base text and are visible only through a truncated patch excerpt (patch_excerpt_complete=false), so they were not fully reviewed.

The base text I did read describes the App Attest endpoint-resumption candidate (A-008/TB-011/T-053), the drain barrier, and the prefix-cache telemetry. It has no code or control changes. The observable doc additions are provider-to-coordinator diagnostics. `detail` is described as 'with consent', carries a busy reason, and is explicitly 'not an authorization or capacity signal', so it adds no authorization surface. `hold_seconds` is a bounded integer (0...86400) with 'invalid_command' validation when `load_model_id` is absent. It is described as a placement hold and not a trust grant, though the described semantics (a positive value replaces an earlier hold) are the only signal I could see.

No finding is supported. Open questions for later passes, if the implementing code is in scope: (1) whether Swift enforces the 0...86400 bound and `invalid_command` rejection for `hold_seconds`; (2) whether the `detail` busy-reason text can leak sensitive local state beyond the closed busy-reason enum, and whether the consent gating is actually enforced in code. Neither can be verified from the supplied evidence. The truncated head sections are the main coverage limit, and deeper review is warranted only if those sections change security claims.
